summary: Iter 30 — Type Revenue Split (Ladies vs Men vs Unisex) — 11/11 backend PASS + all frontend flows PASS on mobile viewport 390x844. Backend: (1) BillItem.service_gender persists explicitly for the 3 bills A/B/C (ladies/men/unisex). (2) Server enrichment works — 4th bill sent with only service_id (no service_gender) is enriched to 'ladies' via _enrich_items_with_service_gender. (3) GET /api/reports/revenue-by-gender?preset=today returns exact shape {from,to,total_revenue,top_segment,segments[]} with total_revenue=1900.0, top_segment='ladies', ladies=1200/2/63.2%, men=300/1/15.8%, unisex=400/1/21.1%; share_pct sums to 100.1 (within 0.5 tolerance). (4) Custom range preset=custom&from_date=<yesterday>&to_date=<today> returns same aggregation over the window; invalid dates -> 400. (5) Empty range (2000-01-01..2000-01-31) returns total_revenue=0, top_segment=null, all segments zero with share_pct=0. (6) Staff scoping — teststaffui GET /reports/revenue-by-gender returns 200 (no 403); segments length=3, revenue >= 0, no branch leakage (staff-branch-scoped bills only). Frontend (owner, mobile 390x844): (A) After seeding 4 test bills via API, Daily Report → 'Today' preset renders the new 'Revenue by Segment' card BETWEEN the totals summary (cardTop=300px) and the daily rows (dayTop=495px). Card header 'Revenue by Segment' with people-circle icon + top-right trophy badge 'Top: Ladies' both present. 3 rows visible with testIDs rev-gender-ladies ('Ladies · 2 items ₹1,200 63.2%'), rev-gender-men ('Men · 1 items ₹300 15.8%'), rev-gender-unisex ('Unisex · 1 items ₹400 21.1%'), each with colored dot and share-pct progress bar (Ladies pink #D9337B, Men blue #2E6BE6, Unisex brand). (B) 'Last Month' preset (no bills in that window) → revenue-by-gender-empty visible with 'No segmented revenue yet — tag services with Ladies / Men / Unisex' text, no crash, revenue-by-gender-card hidden. (C) End-to-end integration validated via the 4th seeded bill that omitted service_gender — server enriched it and it aggregated correctly into ladies bucket (ladies count went 1→2 and revenue 600→1200, verified in UI). All 4 test bills + 3 test services CLEANED UP via API after screenshots.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/reports.py revenue_by_gender: buckets are hardcoded to {ladies, men, unisex} and any unknown value gets coerced to 'unisex' (line 319-320). Fine today because ServiceIn already restricts gender to those 3 literals, but if a future migration adds a new option (e.g. 'kids'), those lines will silently misattribute revenue. Consider using a Literal-derived list to stay in sync with the model.

routes/reports.py:290-291 custom-preset default when no from_date/to_date differs from /reports/range (which defaults both to today). revenue_by_gender defaults from_date to first-of-month and to_date to today. This is a behavioural inconsistency — either both should default to first-of-month or both to today, otherwise sharing the same picker UI can lead to subtle differences.

routes/reports.py:307 uses '<' upper bound with time '23:59:59.999999+00:00' but the '$lt' + max-microsecond string comparison excludes bills whose created_at ends in a >23:59:59.999999 timestamp (which shouldn't happen in practice). Consistent with /reports/range but worth flagging; a '$lte' + '{day}T23:59:59.999999Z' or '$lt' + next day is safer.

routes/bills.py _enrich_items_with_service_gender does a single per-request lookup for lines missing gender but does NOT verify the service actually belongs to the calling tenant. It does filter by {tenant_id: tid, id: {$in: missing_ids}} — good. Just noting the isolation is correct.

app/manage/report.tsx line 61 uses .catch(() => null) which silently swallows any backend error for the gender endpoint. If /reports/revenue-by-gender starts returning 500, the card just quietly disappears with no toast — consider surfacing a small inline error to help debugging.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter 30 delivered clean. Endpoint /api/reports/revenue-by-gender is stable, staff-scoped, and shares preset semantics with /api/reports/range.
